title: Martha Wright-Reed Just and Reasonable Communications Act of 2022
official_summary:
Martha Wright-Reed Just and Reasonable Communications Act of 2022

This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to ensure that rates and charges for payphone services or other calling devices, including advanced (e.g., audio or video) communications services in correctional institutions, are just and reasonable. When promulgating regulations or otherwise implementing this act, the FCC (1) may use industry-wide average costs related to providing telephone and advanced communications services, and (2) must consider costs for safety and security measures related to providing communications services in correctional facilities.

summary.headline: This law requires the FCC to make sure rates for phone and video calls in prisons and jails are just and reasonable.
summary.what_it_does: The FCC must ensure that charges for payphones and other calling devices in correctional institutions are just and reasonable, including audio and video calls. When writing rules, the FCC may use industry-wide average costs for providing these services. The FCC must also consider the costs of safety and security measures in correctional facilities.

who_it_affects.group: People held in prisons and jails
who_it_affects.how: The rates they or others pay for phone and video calls from correctional facilities are subject to the FCC's just-and-reasonable standard.

who_it_affects.group: Families and friends who call incarcerated people
who_it_affects.how: The prices they pay to talk with loved ones in correctional facilities are subject to the same standard.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that provide calling services in correctional facilities
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the FCC's rate rules, which may account for industry-wide average costs and security-related costs.
The agency must write or carry out rules to set and review these rates and must consider security costs when doing so.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The act became law on January 5, 2023, but the official summary does not give a separate start date for the FCC's rules.
